name: Lutetium (177Lu) vipivotide tetraxetan
route_note: IV injection every 6 weeks for up to 6 doses
originator: German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) and Heidelberg University; developed by Endocyte and Novartis

discovery.by: Researchers at DKFZ and Heidelberg University Hospital
discovery.note: PSMA-617 is a small-molecule urea-based PSMA ligand with a DOTA chelator that holds the beta-emitting isotope lutetium-177.

tagline: Radioligand that delivers lutetium-177 beta radiation to PSMA-positive prostate cancer
summary: Lutetium (177Lu) vipivotide tetraxetan is a radiopharmaceutical that binds prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) and delivers beta radiation to prostate cancer cells. It is approved for PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after androgen-receptor pathway inhibition.
mechanism: The PSMA-617 ligand binds the enzymatic pocket of PSMA (FOLH1), which is highly overexpressed on most prostate cancer cells, and the complex is internalised.

Lutetium-177 emits beta particles with a tissue range of under 2 mm, causing DNA damage and death in targeted and nearby cells; it also emits gamma photons that allow imaging. Patients are selected by PSMA PET imaging.
uses: PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after an androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor, either after taxane chemotherapy or when chemotherapy deferral is appropriate

history.title: PSMA-617 described
history.detail: Heidelberg researchers report the theranostic ligand PSMA-617.

history.title: Endocyte licence
history.detail: Endocyte acquires worldwide rights to PSMA-617 from ABX GmbH.

history.title: Novartis acquisition
history.detail: Novartis buys Endocyte for about $2.1 billion.

history.title: VISION trial
history.detail: Added to standard care, it prolongs overall survival in PSMA-positive mCRPC.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in March for PSMA-positive mCRPC after AR-pathway inhibitor and taxane; EU approval in December.

history.title: Pre-chemotherapy use
history.detail: FDA expands the label to patients who have not received taxane chemotherapy (PSMAfore).

pk.half_life: Effective blood half-life ~41 h; physical half-life of 177Lu 6.65 days

facts: Salivary glands express PSMA, explaining dry mouth as a characteristic side effect.
Patient selection uses the matched imaging agent gallium (68Ga) gozetotide or other PSMA PET tracers, an example of theranostics.
